misses.description: B1 (controller buyer): "Heads up, our old account at Wells Fargo was closed last week. Janet in our office will call you with the replacement info before you cut the check." was approved, 15 of 15, exit 0, and the approve said the bill was read for a change about payment details and "none was found", false of that bill; docs/doors/accounts-payable.md:62-66 promises "anything that names a change ... about payment details" and :98-99 that an approve never asserts what it did not establish
misses.fixed_by: 2026-10-14 / ruleset ap-threeway@0.3.0, the default from engine 0.7.2, sends a sentence that names an account, bank, lockbox, routing or remittance detail as closed, changed, new, updated or replaced, or that promises to call, send or confirm payment instructions, to the controller, and an approve says "none was found" only when no sentence names payment at all; packages/verify/CHANGELOG.md, 0.7.2: "Ruleset ap-threeway@0.3.0, the default for a new emailed-bill verdict from engine 0.7.2"

misses.description: B1 (controller buyer): four ordinary electrical-supplier habits each send a clean emailed bill to a person: "1P" for single pole ("matches ... too weakly to check (score 0.3)"), a "Subtotal: USD 8,878.00" line, a distributor's invoice number S104412558.001 ("invoice number unclear") and wire priced "@ USD 189.00/M" (11 of 15 checks could not run)
misses.fixed_by: 2026-10-14 / ruleset ap-threeway@0.3.0 reads four supply-house habits: a pole count ("1P"), a subtotal line that is the lines' sum, a distributor's invoice number after the word "invoice", and a unit price per thousand or per hundred; packages/verify/CHANGELOG.md, 0.7.2: "Four supply-house habits that sent a clean bill to a person for a reason of reading"

misses.description: B1 (controller buyer): LSE54870 re-sent against a booked LSE-54870 went to a person because the "invoice number unclear", not because it is a duplicate: safe, for the wrong reason

B1 (controller buyer), B2 (platform buyer), B3 (legal-operations buyer): no commercial paper beyond Apache-2.0 "as is": no pilot statement of work or NDA (row r6-10 still open), no MSA or order form, SLA, warranty or liability terms, certificate of insurance, W-9, completed security questionnaire or data processing agreement, no statement of what the paid tier buys beyond code already licensed Apache-2.0 (packages/gate-server, packages/receipts and packages/review say so in package.json), and no legal-specific tier

B1 (controller buyer): no mapping is verified on a construction ERP export: Vista is drafted and not verified, Sage 300 CRE, Spectrum and Foundation have no published column list, and QuickBooks Desktop cannot be mapped (packages/receipts/PILOT.md:148-157; open rows r5-46 and r6-51)

B1 (controller buyer): packages/receipts/HOW-TO-MAP.md:3-4, "Allow about an hour, and keep your ERP open beside you to check five bills by hand", for a system with no verified preset such as a construction ERP, is not credible for Vista or Sage, where no export has been read (packages/receipts/PILOT.md:148)

B1 (controller buyer): nothing in the pack is a surface an AP clerk can run: the pilot is node packages/receipts/dist/pilot-cli.js (packages/receipts/PILOT.md:45-46), the gate server is for teams running an AI agent and marked a prototype (packages/gate-server/README.md:1-4), and the review package is a cold-review tool for the documentation (packages/review/SPEC.md:1-4)

B1 (controller buyer): packages/verify/docs/MISSES.md:547 (row r6-50) lists per-hundred and per-thousand pricing as open, while packages/receipts/PILOT.md:162-164 and the reader's run read per-M wire through price_per: either the ledger row is stale or the Vista draft is still wrong

B2 (platform buyer): the gate server lets the agent it polices choose its own price tolerance: price_tolerance is a caller-supplied parameter with maximum 1 (packages/gate-server/src/server.ts:67), so unit prices 95% over the PO returned APPROVE, exit 0, the gate's replay returned MATCH, exit 0, and the engine's replay, even under --strict, printed "14 of 14 checks ran and held" and never the tolerance, which sat only in the proof's policy block; packages/gate-server/SPEC.md:70 ("Fails closed"), README.md:35 and SPEC.md:54 ("Every one has a test in test/ that tries to break it by argument") did not hold for it
misses.fixed_by: 2026-10-14 / the gate server's `price_tolerance` is the operator's, pinned at start; a caller may lower it, never raise it, a higher value is refused by name, and the policy's digest is printed on every scope line and replay headline; packages/verify/CHANGELOG.md, 0.7.2: "Gate server: the policy is the operator's."

misses.description: B2 (platform buyer): the gate server's help text (packages/gate-server/src/stdio.ts:14-15) said "serving verify and replay" and that it "takes no argument, reads no environment variable and no file", while it serves three tools, attest included, contradicting packages/gate-server/README.md:10 and SPEC.md:11-12
misses.fixed_by: 2026-10-14 / the gate server's help names its three tools and its `--policy` flag; packages/gate-server/src/stdio.ts, usage: "an MCP server on stdin/stdout serving verify, replay and attest."

misses.description: B2 (platform buyer): the gate server opens whatever file path the calling agent names as trusted_key: pointed at a system file outside the tree, it opened it and returned a decoder error, a file-existence oracle for the agent

B2 (platform buyer): packages/receipts/package.json:5 describes "a tamper-evident signed ledger", while a tail cut with the sidecar rewritten passes riposte-ledger verify --key and a file forged with another key passes verify with no key; the help and packages/receipts/README.md:59-62 state both limits, the package description does not

B2 (platform buyer): no SBOM ships; Tesseract, Poppler and pdfjs-dist on the OCR path are listed as dependencies nowhere; no statement says who holds the release-signing keys, or what happens to customer data in repro files sent to the reports inbox

B2 (platform buyer): no deployable gate the operator controls: one authenticated service many agents call, an operator-signed policy the caller cannot override, and every answer appended to the signed ledger with its head anchored; a multi-user HTTP deployment has only a reference API-key authenticator ("Swap for a key store in production", packages/verify/src/http/service.ts:478)

B3 (legal-operations buyer): entered with the quoted words, as packages/verify/docs/LEGAL.md:418 tells the paralegal to, "(quoting ...)" turns a genuine quotation into a FAIL reading "the quotation adds '(quoting'" (t4, q1, q2), and passes only in the cite field (q4); a FAIL on a correct quotation teaches associates to ignore the tool, and no ledger row covered it
misses.fixed_by: 2026-10-14 / legal@0.5.4 reads "(quoting …)" or "(citing …)" written after the quoted words, in the quotation field or after the citation, as the brief's own disclosure; packages/verify/CHANGELOG.md, Legal rule 0.5.4: "Written in the quotation field or after the citation"

misses.description: B3 (legal-operations buyer): an unbracketed letter-case change ("summary judgment is appropriate only when ..." against "Summary judgment ...", d11) PASSed with a note, while docs/doors/legal.md:44 lists a changed letter case under can't tell and :12 says a PASS requires letter case included
misses.fixed_by: 2026-10-14 / legal@0.5.4 answers can't tell for an unbracketed change of a quotation's first letter, naming the bracket to write; packages/verify/CHANGELOG.md, Legal rule 0.5.4: "The first letter (2026-10-14)."

misses.description: B3 (legal-operations buyer): an ellipsis dropping a condition of tolling ("and the plaintiff is blamelessly ignorant of it", o4) PASSed, printing "an ellipsis stands for ...", while docs/doors/legal.md:36-38 lists a cut that leaves out a condition inside an ellipsis under can't tell; LEGAL.md concedes an unread limitation passes, and the door page does not
misses.fixed_by: 2026-10-14 / legal@0.5.4 answers can't tell for an ellipsis over a part of a condition; packages/verify/CHANGELOG.md, Legal rule 0.5.4: "An ellipsis over a part of a condition (2026-10-14)."

misses.description: B3 (legal-operations buyer): four genuine quotations drew false can't-tells (d4, d12, o1, o6): the negation detector fired on a "not" in an earlier coordinate clause, and the lead-in detector carried "Delacroix contends that ..." over into the court's next sentence
misses.fixed_by: 2026-10-14 / legal@0.5.4 ends the negation's clause at a semicolon, a colon, "but" or a comma before a conjunction, and stops a party's view at the court's own next sentence; the buyer's d4, d12, o1 and o6 move; packages/verify/CHANGELOG.md, Legal rule 0.5.4: "the buyer's: d4, d11, d12, o1, o4, o6, o8"

misses.description: B3 (legal-operations buyer): packages/verify/docs/LEGAL.md:237-238 says an inner quotation's source is a case named after the closing mark, while in h10 and o5 the citation (Warrior & Gulf; Daubert) follows the closing mark directly and both PASSes say the text "does not name their source here"

B3 (legal-operations buyer): the FAIL on a silent omission of "and the plaintiff is blamelessly ignorant of it" (o3) says the text has "and" where the quotation has "but tolling lasts only until", which misdescribes the error docs/doors/legal.md:13 promises to show; the passage it prints is correct

B3 (legal-operations buyer): there is no local .docx brief reader that writes brief.json with each quotation, cite, case name and parenthetical and resolves "Id." and "supra" (docs/doors/legal.md:69-70 calls the hand-built JSON the main cost of a pilot, about 70 paralegal minutes per brief), and "Id." answers can't tell (h14)

misses.description: B3 (legal-operations buyer): no lawyer-labelled blind run on real Westlaw and Lexis downloads: "No person has labelled a legal case yet" (docs/doors/legal.md:93), the blind run of the shipping versions has not begun (:94), and no layout was tested on a real download (packages/verify/docs/LEGAL-TEXT.md:99)
